breakfast.name: Spaghetti Haitien
instructions: Cook spaghetti
Sauté onion, pepper, garlic, hot dogs in butter
Add ketchup, toss with spaghetti
breakfast.description: Haitian breakfast spaghetti with hot dogs — a beloved morning staple.

breakfast.name: Akasan (Corn Drink)
instructions: Cook cornmeal in water until thick
Add spices, cook 10 min
Strain, add milk and sugar
Serve warm or cold

breakfast.name: Akasan (Cornmeal Drink)
instructions: Cook cornmeal in water, stirring constantly to prevent lumps
Add star anise, cinnamon, lime zest — simmer until thick
Strain through a sieve — push all the liquid through
Add evaporated milk, condensed milk, vanilla
Serve warm or cold — both are traditional
The texture is thick and creamy — almost like a milkshake
Star anise is the signature Haitian spice here — unusual in Caribbean drinks
This is Haiti's morning comfort — nourishing, sweet, warming
breakfast.description: Haiti's cornmeal drink — thick, creamy, sweetened with condensed milk and perfumed with star anise. The star anise is the uniquely Haitian touch that sets akasan apart from every other Caribbean corn drink. A morning ritual and a comfort drink.

breakfast.name: Haitian Spaghetti (Espageti Ayisyen)
instructions: Boil spaghetti until just done
In a pan, sauté onion, garlic, green pepper, Scotch bonnet in butter
Add sliced hot dogs or flaked smoked herring
Add tomato paste or ketchup — this is the sauce
Toss spaghetti into the pan, stir to coat everything
Season with Maggi, salt, pepper
The result is spicy, tomatoey, slightly sweet spaghetti — not Italian at all
This is Haitian breakfast — yes, spaghetti for breakfast — and it's perfect
breakfast.description: Haitian spaghetti — spaghetti tossed with hot dogs, ketchup, and Scotch bonnet for breakfast. Not Italian in any way, and entirely perfect. The 'spaghetti for breakfast' concept and the hot-dog-ketchup-Scotch-bonnet combination shock and delight newcomers every time.

breakfast.name: Labouyi Bannann (Plantain Porridge)
instructions: Grate or blend green plantain with water
Cook the plantain mixture, stirring constantly — it thickens fast
Add cinnamon, star anise, vanilla, nutmeg
Add evaporated and condensed milk
Cook until thick and creamy — 15-20 min
The green plantain gives a starchier, less sweet base than ripe plantain
Serve warm — this is rainy-day, cold-morning comfort food
The star anise and plantain combination is uniquely Haitian
breakfast.description: Haitian plantain porridge — green plantain cooked into a thick, spiced, milky porridge with star anise and cinnamon. The starchy plantain base creates a more substantial porridge than cornmeal. Every Haitian's rainy-morning comfort.

lunch.name: Griot (Fried Pork)
instructions: Marinate pork in sour orange, lime, garlic, spices
Braise in marinade until tender
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve with pikliz and fried plantains
lunch.description: Haiti's national dish — twice-cooked fried pork.

lunch.name: Diri ak Djon Djon (Black Mushroom Rice)
instructions: Soak djon djon in hot water, reserve black liquid
Sauté shallots, garlic, thyme, cloves
Add rice and mushroom liquid
Cook until rice absorbs the dark liquid
lunch.description: Black rice colored by rare Haitian djon djon mushrooms.

lunch.name: Griot (Fried Pork)
ingredients: Sour orange juice (or lime + orange juice mix)
instructions: Marinate pork in sour orange juice, garlic, thyme, parsley, Scotch bonnet, cloves — minimum 2 hours
Boil the pork IN the marinade — yes, boil it first
Cook until tender and all liquid evaporates — 30-40 min
Now fry the boiled pork in oil until crispy on all sides
The boil-then-fry technique is what makes griot: tender inside, crispy outside
Make pikliz while pork fries (pickled cabbage slaw with Scotch bonnet)
Serve griot with pikliz on top and fried plantain on the side
The crispy-tender contrast is the whole point — and it's perfection
Griot is Haiti's celebration food — no party without griot
lunch.description: Haiti's national party food — pork boiled in citrus marinade until tender, then fried until shatteringly crispy. The boil-then-fry technique creates impossible texture: tender-juicy inside, crispy-golden outside. Griot with pikliz (fiery pickled slaw) is the most viral Haitian dish and an absolute masterclass in technique.

lunch.name: Diri ak Djon Djon (Black Mushroom Rice)
ingredients: Djon djon mushrooms (Haitian black mushrooms — only grow in Haiti's north)
instructions: Soak djon djon mushrooms in hot water for 30 min — the water turns jet black
Remove mushrooms, keep the BLACK water — this is the magic
Cook rice in the djon djon water instead of plain water
The rice turns completely black — jet black, dramatic, stunning
Meanwhile, sauté onion, garlic, thyme, add lima beans
Combine with the black rice, add butter, cloves, Scotch bonnet
The flavor of djon djon is earthy, umami, and unlike any other mushroom
The black color comes naturally from the mushroom — no dye, no trick
This rice cannot be made without Haitian djon djon — they don't grow elsewhere
Diri ak djon djon is Haiti's crown jewel — the most distinctive rice dish in the Caribbean
lunch.description: Haiti's iconic black rice — colored jet-black by djon djon mushrooms that only grow in northern Haiti. The mushroom gives an earthy, umami depth that no other rice dish achieves. The dramatic black color and the 'only grows in Haiti' origin story make diri ak djon djon one of the Caribbean's most viral and unique dishes.

lunch.name: Legim (Haitian Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: Epis (Haitian seasoning base: garlic, parsley, green onion, thyme, cloves, pepper)
instructions: Make epis: blend garlic, parsley, green onion, thyme, cloves, Scotch bonnet
Cut all vegetables into chunks
Cook meat in epis until browned
Add tomato paste, fry until dark
Add vegetables in order of cook time: eggplant and carrots first, cabbage and chayote next, greens last
Add butter — the Haitian vegetable stew uses more butter than you'd expect
Simmer until all vegetables are tender but not mushy — 30-40 min
The stew should be thick, rich, and loaded with vegetables
Serve over white rice — the colorful stew on white rice is beautiful
This is Haiti's Saturday food — the whole family eats legim on Saturday
lunch.description: Haiti's vegetable stew — a rich, butter-enriched celebration of every vegetable in the market, cooked with epis (the Haitian seasoning base) and served over rice. Legim is Saturday food — the whole-family, slow-cooking, every-vegetable-in-the-pot tradition.

dinner.name: Poisson Gros Sel (Fish in Coarse Salt)
instructions: Score fish, rub with lime and salt
Marinate in epis 30 min
Deep fry whole until golden and crispy
Serve with plantain and salad
dinner.description: Whole fried fish seasoned with Haitian epis.

dinner.name: Legim (Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Sauté meat or crab
Add all vegetables progressively
Simmer until everything is very soft
Mash lightly
Serve over white rice
dinner.description: Hearty mixed vegetable stew — Haitian comfort food.

dinner.name: Tasso Cabrit (Spiced Fried Goat)
instructions: Marinate goat in sour orange, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, cloves — 2+ hours
Boil goat in the marinade until tender — the same boil-then-fry technique as griot
When tender and liquid has evaporated, fry in oil until crispy and browned
The goat is more intensely flavored than pork — gamey, herby, crispy
Make a quick sauce: sauté onion and Scotch bonnet in the frying oil
Pour the onion sauce over the fried goat
Serve with fried plantain and pikliz
Tasso cabrit is the goat version of griot — for goat lovers, it's even better
The boil-then-fry technique works even better with goat's stronger flavor
dinner.description: Haiti's spiced fried goat — the same boil-then-fry technique as griot applied to goat. The goat's stronger, gamey flavor stands up to the aggressive citrus-spice marinade even better than pork. Tasso cabrit is for when you want griot turned up to 11.

dinner.name: Poisson Gros Sel (Salt-Crusted Fish)
ingredients: Whole red snapper (or any firm white fish)
instructions: Clean fish, score both sides
Rub with lime juice and epis inside and out
Pack the entire fish in coarse salt — completely encased
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 min
Crack the salt crust open — the drama of the reveal is part of the experience
The fish inside is perfectly seasoned, moist, and tender
The salt crust seals in all the moisture and flavor
Remove the salt crust (don't eat it — it's too salty)
Serve the fish with sauce ti-malice (spicy shallot sauce) on the side
The crust-cracking moment is the viral hook
dinner.description: Haitian salt-crusted fish — whole snapper encased in coarse salt and baked until the crust hardens into an armor. The dramatic crust-cracking reveal shows perfectly moist, seasoned fish inside. The theatrical reveal and the ti-malice sauce make this viral Haitian coastal cooking.

dinner.name: Bouillon (Haitian Beef-Vegetable Soup)
instructions: Boil beef with epis until tender — make rich broth
Add root vegetables: yam, malanga, potato — cook 15 min
Add plantain, carrots, celery — cook 10 min
Add cabbage, spinach, pasta — cook 10 min
Add lime juice and butter
The soup should be thick, loaded with vegetables, and deeply flavored
Each bowl should have meat, root vegetables, greens, and pasta
This is Haiti's Saturday night soup — a full meal in a bowl
Every Haitian has a bouillon memory — it's the soup of home
The American Thanksgiving equivalent: family, abundance, comfort
dinner.description: Haiti's everything soup — beef, root vegetables, greens, plantain, and pasta in a rich broth that's a full meal in a bowl. Haitian bouillon is Saturday night family food, a celebration of abundance, and the soup that every Haitian abroad misses most.

snacks.name: Pikliz (Spicy Slaw)
instructions: Toss cabbage, carrots, peppers
Mix vinegar, lime juice, cloves, salt
Pour over vegetables
Let sit 1 hour minimum
snacks.description: Fiery pickled cabbage condiment — served with everything.

snacks.name: Pikliz (Fiery Pickled Slaw)
instructions: Shred cabbage finely, julienne carrots
Slice Scotch bonnet peppers — use more than you think you should
Combine vegetables in a jar
Cover with white vinegar and lime juice
Add cloves, black pepper, salt
Seal tightly — refrigerate at least 24 hours before using
The flavor develops over days — week-old pikliz is better than day-old
The heat level is extreme — this is not a mild condiment
Pikliz goes on everything in Haitian food — griot, fish, rice, sandwiches
Make a big jar — you'll go through it fast
snacks.description: Haiti's fiery pickled slaw — shredded cabbage and carrots drowned in vinegar and Scotch bonnet. Goes on literally everything. Pikliz is the condiment that makes Haitian food Haitian, and the extreme heat level has made it viral as the Caribbean's answer to kimchi.

snacks.name: Pate Kode (Haitian Patties)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, water, salt, sugar
Filling: seasoned beef, chicken, salt cod, or herring
instructions: Make dough: flour, butter, salt, sugar — work until smooth, rest 30 min
Make filling: cook seasoned meat with epis, tomato paste, Scotch bonnet until thick
Roll out dough, cut into circles
Fill with meat mixture, fold into half-moons, seal edges
Deep fry until golden and crispy — 3-4 min
Drain briefly — serve hot
The crust should be flaky and blistered from the frying
These are Haiti's street food — sold at every corner, school gate, and market
The salt cod version (pate kode mori) is the most traditional
snacks.description: Haitian patties — flaky fried dough pockets filled with spiced meat, salt cod, or herring. Haiti's ubiquitous street food — sold at every corner and school gate. The flaky crust and the epis-spiced filling make pate kode one of the Caribbean's best hand-held snacks.

snacks.name: Bannann Peze (Twice-Fried Plantain / Tostones)
ingredients: Garlic water (optional — garlic soaked in salted water)
instructions: Peel green plantains, cut into 1-inch rounds
Fry in hot oil until light golden — 3 min
Remove, smash each piece flat with a tostonera or the bottom of a glass
Dip smashed plantain in garlic water (optional but traditional)
Fry again until golden and crispy — 2-3 min
The double frying creates: first fry cooks the inside, smash increases surface area, second fry crisps everything
Season with salt immediately
Serve alongside griot, fish, or any main dish
The satisfying crunch of well-made bannann peze is unmatched
snacks.description: Haiti's twice-fried plantain — the fry-smash-fry technique that creates maximum crunch. The optional garlic water dip between fries adds savory depth. Bannann peze is the essential Haitian side dish and the twice-frying technique is viral cooking content.

desserts.name: Pain Patate (Sweet Potato Pudding)
instructions: Mix grated sweet potato with coconut milk, sugar, spices
Add mashed banana and raisins
Pour into greased pan
Bake at 160°C 90 min until firm
desserts.description: Dense, sweet, spiced sweet potato pudding.

desserts.name: Pen Patat (Sweet Potato Pudding)
instructions: Grate sweet potatoes finely
Mix with coconut milk, evaporated milk, sugar
Add mashed banana — it adds moisture and sweetness
Add cinnamon, nutmeg, star anise, vanilla, raisins
Add melted butter
Pour into greased baking dish
Bake at 175°C for 50-60 min until firm and golden on top
The pudding should be dense, moist, and custardy — not cakey
The star anise gives the uniquely Haitian aromatic note
Serve warm or cold — the flavors deepen as it cools
desserts.description: Haitian sweet potato pudding — grated sweet potato baked with coconut milk, banana, and star anise into a dense, aromatic, custardy pudding. Star anise is Haiti's signature spice, and pen patat is the dessert that proves it. Rich, warming, and deeply Haitian.

desserts.name: Douce Makòs (Haitian Fudge)
instructions: Combine evaporated milk, condensed milk, sugar, butter in a pot
Cook on medium heat, stirring CONSTANTLY — it scorches easily
Add star anise for steeping — the Haitian touch
Cook until very thick and pulling away from the sides — 15-20 min
Remove star anise, add vanilla and lime zest
Pour onto buttered surface or parchment
Let cool and set — cut into squares
The texture is like fudge — dense, sweet, slightly caramelized
This is Haiti's answer to dulce de leche, toffee, and fudge all at once
Douce makòs is the candy of every Haitian childhood
desserts.description: Haitian fudge — condensed and evaporated milk cooked with star anise until thick and fudgy. Haiti's childhood candy. The star-anise-infused caramel and the fudge-like texture make douce makòs a uniquely Haitian confection.

drinks.name: Kremas (Haitian Egg Nog)
instructions: Simmer milks with spices 5 min
Cool, add rum
Blend until smooth
Bottle, refrigerate
Shake before serving

drinks.name: Jus Papaye (Papaya Juice)
instructions: Blend papaya flesh with water
Add lime, sugar, vanilla
Strain, serve cold

drinks.name: Kremas (Haitian Eggnog/Cream Liqueur)
instructions: Blend coconut cream, condensed milk, evaporated milk
Add rum — be generous, this is a celebration drink
Add vanilla, lime zest, cinnamon, nutmeg, star anise
The star anise is what makes kremas Haitian and not just 'Caribbean eggnog'
Blend until completely smooth and creamy
Bottle and refrigerate — it keeps for weeks (the rum preserves it)
Shake before serving — serve cold
This is Haiti's Christmas drink — no holiday without kremas
Every family has their own recipe — the rum-to-cream ratio is the debate
Kremas is Haiti's answer to coquito, eggnog, and Irish cream
drinks.description: Haiti's celebration cream liqueur — coconut cream, condensed milk, and Barbancourt rum with star anise. The Haitian Christmas drink that rivals Puerto Rican coquito and American eggnog. Every family's recipe is 'the best' and the rum-to-cream ratio debate is annual. Star anise makes it uniquely Haitian.

drinks.name: Jus Papay (Papaya Juice)
instructions: Scoop ripe papaya flesh, remove seeds
Blend with water or evaporated milk
Add sugar, lime juice, vanilla
Blend until smooth
Strain if desired — some prefer it smooth, some pulpy
Serve very cold
The color is a beautiful sunset orange
Papaya juice with milk is like a tropical milkshake
Fresh papaya is abundant in Haiti — this is the simplest use of the fruit
drinks.description: Haitian papaya juice — ripe papaya blended into a sunset-orange drink with lime and vanilla. Made creamy with evaporated milk or refreshing with just water. Haiti's fruit abundance in liquid form.
